findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: The authenticated-user check only runs when an `Integration` already exists without an `OrganizationIntegration`. If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to anything. The `Integration` row is normally created by the `installation` webhook, so until that webhook is processed (or if it is delayed or lost) any user who completes the OAuth step can claim any `installation_id`. `build_integration` then fetches the installation with the app JWT and creates the integration, and `state['sender']` is never set. This is the attack the PR is meant to stop, and the validation does not cover it. A stronger check would verify with GitHub, using the user's OAuth token, that the user can access that installation.

findings.title: KeyError (HTTP 500) when stored Integration has no `sender` metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the key always exists. `build_integration` only sets `metadata['sender']` when `state.get('sender')` is truthy, and nothing in this pipeline sets it. Integrations created through the pipeline, or before the webhook started recording the sender, have no `sender` key. If such an Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration, the lookup raises `KeyError` and the user gets a 500 instead of the friendly error. Use `.get()` chains and treat a missing sender as a failed validation.

findings.title: Network failures in token exchange and user lookup are not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the `try` block, so connection errors, SSL errors and timeouts reach the user as a 500. `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token`, which this code copies, wraps the request in a `try`. Likewise `get_user_info` (line 434) is not guarded and, as far as I recall, calls `raise_for_status()`, so a GitHub 4xx/5xx raises instead of reaching the `'login' not in ...` check. These failures should produce the same 'could not verify the installation request' error as the other failure paths.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding its parameters
findings.body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are not percent-encoded. The existing `OAuth2LoginView` uses `urlencode`. An unencoded `redirect_uri` that contains a port, query or special characters can be mangled or rejected by GitHub. The test asserts the unencoded form, which locks in this behaviour. Build the query with `urlencode`.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The test stubs a 404 for `/app/installations/{id}`, but it now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`. The pipeline signature in the other tests is `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`, so this request fails the new state check in `OAuthLoginView`. The installation lookup is never reached. The assertion was changed from 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to the generic 'Invalid installation request.', which hides the fact that the original behaviour is no longer covered. The 404 handling in `build_integration` has no test, and the state-mismatch case is only tested by accident under a misleading name. Use the correct state in this test so it reaches `build_integration`, and add a separate state-mismatch test.

findings.title: Missing tests for the success path and the new OAuth failure modes
findings.body: Only the user-mismatch rejection is tested. There is no test where an Integration already exists (created by the webhook) with `sender.login` matching the authenticated user and the install succeeds. There are also no deliberate tests for a wrong `state`, a failed `access_token` exchange (for example `error=bad_verification_code`), a `/user` response without `login`, or an Integration whose metadata lacks `sender`. These are the behaviours listed in the PR description, and the last case would currently hit the `KeyError`.
